proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(t_n=\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\), and let \(\underline v\) be the constant in Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\). Compactness of \(\mathcal X\) supplies a finite bound \(B\) for every coordinate of \(V\) and for every clipped residual used below. Constants denoted by \(K\), \(K_R\), and \(K_H\) may depend on \(B\), the fixed fold proportions, the Holder radius, the two design-density bounds, the kernel bounds, and \(L_k\), but not on \(n\), \(\alpha\), or the indices \((v,A,u)\).

First construct the regression fits. Fix \(v\in I\), \(A\subseteq I\setminus\{v\}\), and put \(m=|A|\). Partition \(\mathcal X_A\) into rectangles of side at most \(h\), use polynomials of total degree at most two on each nonempty rectangle, and clip their values to the coordinate range of \(V_v\). Taylor's formula and Assumption \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\) give a sieve member \(g_h\) satisfying
\[
 \lVert g_h-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_\infty\le K h^3. \tag{1}
\]
There are at most \(K h^{-m}\) polynomial coefficients. The empirical least-squares basic inequality gives the following bound. Indeed, bounded squared-loss differences have conditional variance at most a constant times their excess squared-error risk; on a shell with population excess risk \(r\), exponential Markov's inequality and a finite-dimensional net for the \(K h^{-m}\) coefficients give an upper probability \(\exp\{-c n r+K h^{-m}\}\). Peeling over dyadic shells, using (1) as the comparison element, and summing the geometric series gives, for the clipped least-squares fit on a training fold of size proportional to \(n\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left{
 \lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}^2
 >K\left(h^6+\frac{h^{-m}+\log(1/\delta)}{n}\right)
 \right}\le\delta . \tag{2}
\]
Thus (2) uses boundedness, Assumptions \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\) and \(\ref{ass:design-density}\), and the independent training sample supplied by Assumption \(\ref{ass:iid-sampling}\); no additional moment or tail premise is used.

Take \(h=t_n^{1/(m+6)}\) when \(t_n\le1\), and allocate failure probability proportional to \(\alpha/M_d\). Since \(m\le d-1\),
\[
 t_n^{3/(m+6)}\le t_n^{3/(d+5)}=a_n.
\]
A union bound over the \(d2^{d-1}\) regressions yields
\[
 \max_{v,A}\lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}
 \le K a_n. \tag{3}
\]
When \(t_n>1\), clipping and enlargement of \(K\) give (3) directly because both the response and the fitted regression are bounded. Repeating the argument over the fixed number of cross-fitting folds changes only \(K\).

On an evaluation fold independent of a fitted regression, let \(\widehat R_{v,A}\) be the empirical mean of the squared fitted residual. The orthogonality of conditional expectation in Definition \(\ref{def:conditional-risk}\) gives, conditionally on the training fold,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[(V_v-\widehat\mu_{v,A}(V_A))^2\mid\widehat\mu_{v,A}\right]
 =R_{v,A}+\lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}^2. \tag{4}
\]
The evaluation losses are conditionally independent and bounded. If a centered random variable \(W\) satisfies \(|W|\le b\), convexity of the exponential on \([-b,b]\) gives \(\mathbb E e^{sW}\le e^{s^2b^2/2}\). Exponential Markov optimization and a union bound therefore give simultaneous evaluation error at most \(K\sqrt{t_n}\). Combining this with (3)--(4) produces risk intervals containing all \(R_{v,A}\), with common half-width
\[
 w_R\le K_R\{t_n^{1/2}+a_n^2\}
 =K_R\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}. \tag{5}
\]

For an HSIC coordinate, use the bounded centered order-four V-statistic on an evaluation fold with off-fold residuals. Conditional on the training fold, changing one evaluation observation changes this statistic by at most \(K/n\). Exposing observations one at a time and applying the preceding exponential argument gives deviation \(K\sqrt{t_n}\); repeated-index terms contribute at most \(K/n\), which is absorbed by that bound. To compare fitted- and true-residual population HSIC, expand HSIC as a fixed finite sum of expectations of products of bounded kernel factors, telescope each product at its residual-kernel factor, and apply Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\). Cauchy--Schwarz and (3) give
\[
 \left|H_{\widehat\mu}(v,A,u)-H(v,A,u)\right|
 \le K\mathbb E_P\left|\widehat\mu_{v,A}(V_A)-\mu_{v,A}(V_A)\right|
 \le K a_n. \tag{6}
\]
There are \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant coordinates \(H(v,A,u)\) with \(u\in A\). The pruning coordinates have the form \(H(v,A,u)\) with \(u\notin A\), and there are at most another \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) such coordinates. Hence simultaneous intervals cover both tables and have common half-width
\[
 w_H\le K_H\{t_n^{1/2}+a_n\}
 =K_H\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}. \tag{7}
\]
Adding the pruning table changes the number of controlled quantities from \(M_d\) to at most \(2M_d\). Since \(M_d/\alpha\ge2\), \(\log(2M_d/\alpha)\le2\log(M_d/\alpha)\), so this change is absorbed into \(K_H\). Allocating the regression, risk-evaluation, and HSIC failure probabilities to sum to at most \(\alpha\) proves the simultaneous coverage event, denoted below by \(\mathcal E_n\), and the bounds (5) and (7).

We next derive the score radius. Work on \(\mathcal E_n\), suppose the set-valued decision has fixed every score-relevant dependence indicator under consideration at its true singleton value, and assume \(w_R<\underline v/2\). Write
\[
 y_v=R_{v,\varnothing}=\operatorname{Var}_P(V_v),
 \qquad x_{v,A}=R_{v,A}.
\]
Conditional expectation is the \(L^2(P)\) projection onto functions of \(V_A\). Definition \(\ref{def:conditional-risk}\) and Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\) therefore imply
\[
 0\le x_{v,A}\le y_v,
 \qquad y_v\ge\underline v. \tag{8}
\]
Let \(\widehat y_v\) and \(\widehat x_{v,A}\) be risk-band centers, and project \(\widehat x_{v,A}\) onto \([0,\widehat y_v]\), calling the result \(\widetilde x_{v,A}\). Coverage and \(w_R<\underline v/2\) imply \(\widehat y_v>0\). If \(x_{v,A}\le\widehat y_v\), projection onto an interval containing \(x_{v,A}\) cannot increase error. If \(x_{v,A}>\widehat y_v\), then \(0<x_{v,A}-\widehat y_v\le y_v-\widehat y_v\le w_R\). Thus
\[
 |\widetilde x_{v,A}-x_{v,A}|\le w_R,
 \qquad |\widehat y_v-y_v|\le w_R. \tag{9}
\]
Define \(\widetilde q(v,A)=1-\widetilde x_{v,A}/\widehat y_v\). From (8)--(9), \(0\le\widetilde x_{v,A}/\widehat y_v\le1\), and Definition \(\ref{def:correlation-ratio}\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\widetilde q(v,A)-q(v,A)|
 &=\left|\frac{x_{v,A}}{y_v}-\frac{\widetilde x_{v,A}}{\widehat y_v}\right|\\
 &\le \frac{|x_{v,A}-\widetilde x_{v,A}|}{y_v}
 +\frac{\widetilde x_{v,A}}{\widehat y_v}\frac{|\widehat y_v-y_v|}{y_v}
 \le \frac{2w_R}{\underline v}. \tag{10}
\end{aligned}
\]
With singleton dependence labels, the multiplier \(1-D(v,A)/(|A|+1)\) in Definition \(\ref{def:gene-score}\) belongs to \([0,1]\). An insertion changes predecessor sets only for the moved node and the traversed block, hence for at most \(d\) nodes. Its gain is the difference between the before and after local contributions of precisely those nodes. Applying (10) to both contributions for each affected node gives
\[
 w_S\le \frac{4d}{\underline v}w_R. \tag{11}
\]
This argument does not assert continuity of the independence indicator: (11) is conditional on the relevant labels being fixed at their true singleton values.

We now separate the two HSIC promises needed for confidence-set coverage and singleton recovery. Let \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{ex}}\) be the finite set of score and pruning HSIC coordinates actually queried along the exact population execution in Definition \(\ref{def:oracle-recovery}\), and let \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{all}}(\mathcal B)\) be the union of the score and pruning HSIC coordinates queryable along any execution compatible with the realized bands \(\mathcal B\) of Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\).

Suppose \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\) and
\[
 H(\xi)\in\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)
 \quad\text{for every }\xi\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{ex}}. \tag{12}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_n\), a queried true value \(H=0\) makes the intersected HSIC interval contain \(0\), so the set-valued rule includes \(\mathrm{ind}\); a queried true value \(H\ge\lambda\) makes the intersection meet \([\lambda,\infty)\), so the rule includes \(\mathrm{dep}\). Thus every true dependence label along the exact execution is retained, irrespective of \(w_H\). Every true risk is also retained. Interval extension through Definition \(\ref{def:correlation-ratio}\) therefore retains the exact \(q(v,A)\) and insertion gains; when a denominator interval meets zero, enlarging its image to the known range \([0,1]\) still retains the true value. Hence the exact population execution is compatible with the bands. Theorem \(\ref{thm:oracle-recovery}\) says that its terminal graph is \(G_0\), while Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\) takes the union of all compatible terminal DAGs. Consequently \(G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\) on \(\mathcal E_n\), and
\[
 \Pr_P\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\}\ge1-\alpha. \tag{13}
\]
Notice that (12) concerns only the exact population path; it makes no assertion about HSIC coordinates reached solely by other compatible paths.

For singleton recovery, impose the stronger, realized-path promise
\[
 H(\xi)\in\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)
 \quad\text{for every }\xi\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{all}}(\mathcal B), \tag{14}
\]
and continue on \(\mathcal E_n\). Assume also \(2w_H<\lambda\). If a coordinate in (14) has \(H=0\), its band after intersection with the nonnegative line has upper endpoint at most \(2w_H<\lambda\); if it has \(H\ge\lambda\), its lower endpoint is at least \(H-2w_H>0\). Therefore every HSIC label on every compatible path is the correct singleton label. If in addition \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\), Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) supplies, at each non-topological order reached on any compatible path, a correcting insertion with true gain at least \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\). Its propagated lower endpoint is greater than \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}-2w_S>0\), so no compatible execution can terminate at that order. A compatible score table strictly increases at every move and the permutation set is finite, so every compatible terminal order is topological. By (14), its pruning labels coincide with the population labels. Theorem \(\ref{thm:oracle-recovery}\) then gives terminal graph \(G_0\) on every compatible path, and hence
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}. \tag{15}
\]
The strengthening from (12) to (14) is essential to this argument: separation solely along the exact path does not determine labels on a different path admitted by the bands.

It remains to verify the direct margins and sample-size order. Choose
\[
 K_1\ge \frac{8K_R}{\underline v},
 \qquad K_2\ge2K_H, \tag{16}
\]
enlarging them only to absorb the fixed regularity and fold constants. Since \(d\ge2\) and \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\le1\),
\[
 K_1d\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}} \tag{17}
\]
and (5) imply \(w_R<\underline v/2\). Equations (5), (11), and (16)--(17) then imply \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\). Likewise,
\[
 K_2\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}<\lambda \tag{18}
\]
and (7), (16) imply \(2w_H<\lambda\). Thus (14), (17), and (18) imply (15).

Finally fix the regularity constants and suppose \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}},\lambda\le1\). Put
\[
 \gamma_d=\max\left\{2,\frac{d+5}{6}\right\},
 \qquad \beta_d=\frac{d+5}{3}.
\]
Because \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}/d\le1\), taking \(t_n\) no larger than a sufficiently small constant multiple of \((\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}/d)^{\gamma_d}\) controls both terms in (17). Since \(\beta_d>2\) for \(d\ge2\), taking \(t_n\) no larger than a sufficiently small constant multiple of \(\lambda^{\beta_d}\) controls both terms in (18). It is therefore sufficient that
\[
 n\ge K\log(M_d/\alpha)
 \max\left\{
 \left(\frac d{\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}}\right)^{\max\{2,(d+5)/6\}},
 \lambda^{-(d+5)/3}
 \right\}. \tag{19}
\]
The score-margin exponent is two for \(d<7\), the two powers coincide at \(d=7\), and \((d+5)/6\) governs for \(d>7\). Equation (19) is sufficient; no minimax optimality is claimed.

If the singleton width conditions and the all-compatible-query promise (14) are not imposed, an HSIC interval may retain both \(\mathrm{ind}\) and \(\mathrm{dep}\). Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\) then returns the union of compatible terminal DAGs, which may be a singleton or may contain multiple graphs. This conclusion does not weaken the coverage guarantee (13), whose weaker promise is only (12).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Under Assumptions \(\ref{ass:iid-sampling}\), \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\), \(\ref{ass:design-density}\), \(\ref{ass:characteristic-kernels}\), and \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\), there are finite constants \(K,K_1,K_2\), depending only on the fixed regularity and fold constants, such that, with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), all \(d2^{d-1}\) conditional risks, all \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant residual-HSIC coordinates, and every residual-HSIC coordinate that can be queried by pruning lie in their cross-fitted bands, with \(w_R\le K\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}\) and \(w_H\le K\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}\), where \(t_n=\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\) and \(a_n=t_n^{3/(d+5)}\). Bounded kernels control the held-out HSIC fluctuation, and Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\) is used only to turn cross-fitted residual error into the additive \(a_n\) term. On this simultaneous event, whenever the score-relevant dependence labels under consideration are fixed at their true singleton values and \(w_R<\underline v/2\), \(w_S\le4d w_R/\underline v\). If \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\) and every score or pruning HSIC coordinate queried along the exact population execution belongs to \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\), then \(\Pr_P\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\), without any width requirement. Singleton recovery requires the stronger promise that every score and pruning HSIC coordinate queryable by any execution compatible with the realized bands belongs to \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\); under that promise, \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) and \(2w_H<\lambda\) imply \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}\). The direct inequalities \(K_1d\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) and \(K_2\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}<\lambda\) imply these width inequalities. For fixed regularity constants and \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}},\lambda\le1\), it is sufficient that \(n\ge K\log(M_d/\alpha)\max\{(d/\delta_{\mathrm{pair}})^{\max\{2,(d+5)/6\}},\lambda^{-(d+5)/3}\}\). The score-margin exponent has its elbow at \(d=7\); this sufficient order is not claimed to be minimax optimal. If the singleton width conditions and the all-compatible-query separation promise are not imposed, the set-valued rule retains both labels whenever warranted and the compatible-DAG union may be a singleton or may contain multiple graphs.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The previous claim used an ambiguous phrase, every queried HSIC value, for both coverage and singleton recovery. Exact-path separation is sufficient to retain the true oracle execution and hence gives honest graph-set coverage without width conditions, but it does not separate labels on other compatible paths. Singleton recovery therefore needs the stronger all-compatible-query separation promise in addition to the score and HSIC width inequalities. The replacement also records the already-proved score-radius bound, direct margins, sufficient sample-size order, dimension-seven elbow, and no-minimax qualification.

prose_updates.tldr: For the exact \(\alpha=1\) population-oracle analogue of GENE Equation (6), a primitive edgewise inequality on support-closed matching-component additive-noise models forces a positive reversal-correcting insertion at every wrong order, so best improvement and independence pruning recover the labelled DAG with a finite oracle-query budget. This is a certified success region, not a theorem for Li et al.'s full nonlinear class. For every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), an explicitly parameterized relatively open bivariate family, including a nonempty relatively open non-affine subfamily, makes the identifiable causal model \(X\to Y\) have the wrong order as its unique global and hence insertion-local maximizer with score advantage strictly greater than \(\eta\); the universal sharp supremum is \(1/2\). Cross-fitted simultaneous bands abstain at unresolved independence labels; on separated score labels, \(w_S\le4d w_R/\underline v\), and direct margin inequalities yield the sufficient sample size \(n\gtrsim\log(M_d/\alpha)\max\{(d/\delta_{\mathrm{pair}})^{\max\{2,(d+5)/6\}},\lambda^{-(d+5)/3}\}\), with the score-margin elbow at \(d=7\) and no minimax claim. Under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\), HSIC separation only for the score and pruning coordinates on the exact population execution suffices for \(1-\alpha\) coverage of \(G_0\) without width conditions. Singleton recovery additionally requires separation for every coordinate queryable by any compatible execution and the score and HSIC width inequalities; without those stronger conditions, the compatible-DAG union may be singleton or multiple.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The success certificate is sufficient only on matching-component DAGs and is not an observable necessary-and-sufficient boundary for general GENE landscapes. The sharp bivariate construction proves a margin-indexed relatively open failure region, including a relatively open non-affine subfamily, inside the identifiable nonlinear-ANM class and attains the universal one-half supremum only as a limit; it does not classify the intervening general class. Exact independence remains discontinuous: the population trap handles it pointwise by support geometry throughout its open structural family, while finite-sample inference uses set-valued labels. Under the matching class, separation only for score and pruning coordinates on the exact population execution makes that true execution compatible and gives \(\mathbb P\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) even when widths are large. It does not separate coordinates reached only by alternative compatible paths. Singleton recovery therefore requires the stronger all-compatible-query separation promise as well as \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) and \(2w_H<\lambda\); absent those conditions, the compatible-DAG union may be singleton or multiple. The residual-estimation contribution to the HSIC radius uses the stated nonstandard residual-coordinate Lipschitz premise. The displayed sample-size order suppresses fixed regularity constants and is sufficient, not minimax optimal.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The delivered population results are a compact-support identification bridge, a matching-subclass insertion-navigation theorem, a six-node strict separation witness, finite-query oracle recovery, a quadratic positive-gain witness, and, for every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), a sharp relatively open bivariate trapped-order family with a nonempty relatively open non-affine subfamily. The wrong order is the unique global and hence insertion-local maximizer by more than \(\eta\), while the universal supremum of this score advantage is \(1/2\). The matching-subclass theorem does not establish success on Li et al.'s full nonlinear class; the nonlinear witnesses transfer to that class only existentially, and the trap does not contradict Theorem 4.3 because its global-ranking premise fails there. The simultaneous-band theorem gives \(w_S\le4d w_R/\underline v\) on separated score labels when \(w_R<\underline v/2\), direct sufficient conditions \(K_1d\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) and \(K_2\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}<\lambda\), where \(t_n=\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\), and the \(d=7\) score-rate elbow. Under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\), HSIC separation on the exact population execution alone yields \(\mathbb P\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) without width inequalities. Singleton recovery requires both width inequalities and the stronger promise separating every score and pruning coordinate queryable along any compatible execution; otherwise the compatible-DAG union may be singleton or multiple. No minimax rate, observable general-class boundary, or claim against Li et al. Theorem 4.3 is made. The released Sachs workflow remains an audit case: a fixed chi-square threshold does not certify a population margin, and intervention-informed reference directions do not follow from an observational acyclic ANM alone.
